04 Anxiety and benzodiazepines · class card

Other anxiety agents

buspirone · hydroxyzine · gabapentin · pregabalin

Key point
  • Buspirone: serotonin 1A partial agonist
  • Buspirone: no sedation, no tolerance or addiction, no alcohol interaction
  • Generalized anxiety disorder: buspirone is second line, alone or as an add-on
  • Buspirone add-on: used when a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) or serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (SNRI) falls short
  • Hydroxyzine: sedating first-generation antihistamine
  • Hydroxyzine: short-term add-on while the SSRI or SNRI is titrated
  • Older adult: hydroxyzine anticholinergic action can lead to delirium
  • Buspirone: does not treat obsessive-compulsive disorder
  • Buspirone: gives no cover for benzodiazepine withdrawal
Drugs

: not related to benzodiazepines or barbiturates Buspirone clearanceCleared by cytochrome P450 3A4Avoid large amounts of grapefruit juice

Hydroxyzine: a first-generation antihistamine, as are meclizine and promethazine MnemonicAntihistamine mnemonicThe "-zine" ending marks these first-generation antihistamines.

Gabapentin Neurontin: a gabapentinoid that resembles gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) but does not act like it

Pregabalin Lyrica: the same mechanism as gabapentin

Mechanism

Serotonin 1A receptors partially stimulated () anxiety eased without the sedation of typical anxiolytics Buspirone mnemonicAnxious when the bus does not arrive at oneBuspirone acts at serotonin 1A

Histamine 1 receptors blocked (hydroxyzine) drowsiness; anticholinergic action dry mouth

Alpha-2-delta subunit bound (gabapentinoids) voltage-gated calcium channels blocked

Uses

: generalized anxiety disorder, second line, alone or as an add-on; taken on a schedule, no rescue dose Buspirone dosingIn practice: anxiety symptoms typically ease only once the dose reaches the upper range ⚠︎ pharm document line; no board source found yet

Buspirone: does not treat obsessive-compulsive disorder or somatic symptom disorder

: a short-term add-on for severe anxiety, agitation or insomnia during SSRI or SNRI titration Hydroxyzine usesAlso listed: itching from allergic conditions such as chronic urticaria

Pregabalin: generalized anxiety disorder, second line

Gabapentin: often used as an add-on for anxiety, sleep and neuropathic pain ⚠︎ pharm document line; no board source found yet

Gabapentin for anxiety: off-label

Adverse effects

Buspirone: dizziness, nausea, headache, nervousness; no sedation, no dependence

: drowsiness, dry mouth Hydroxyzine and QTContraindicated with a prolonged QT intervalQT prolongation and torsades de pointes have been reportedUse caution with other QT-prolonging drugs

Hydroxyzine in older adults: possible confusion, delirium (see Anticholinergic delirium below) and falls ⚠︎ pharm document line; no board source found yet

: sedation, ataxia, dizziness, peripheral edema Gabapentin dosingReduced kidney function: gabapentin dose is adjusted

Pregabalin: sedation, weight gain

Anticholinergic deliriumAn older adult on hydroxyzine turns drowsy and confused, with a dry mouth

If an older adult needs an add-on for anxiety or sleep, choose an option other than a first-generation antihistamine such as hydroxyzine.

Drug interactions
DrugEffectManagement
No added impairmentFits a patient who drinks, unlike a benzodiazepine Buspirone and alcoholIn practice: avoid alcohol with buspironeNo added impairment was found with alcohol
Alcohol or another central nervous system depressant, with hydroxyzineAdded sedationAvoid together

Practice
  1. 45-year-old man with generalized anxiety disorder, partly better after 10 weeks of sertraline alcohol use disorder, sober 1 year; drives a delivery truck wants an add-on that will not sedate him or become habit-forming examination normal → Add buspirone → buspirone, a partial agonist at serotonin 1A receptors, may be added when the response to an SSRI falls short and brings no sedation, tolerance or addiction; benzodiazepines carry risks of addiction and dependence, which he asked to avoid, and hydroxyzine is a sedating short-term add-on
  2. 34-year-old woman with generalized anxiety disorder, partly better on escitalopram an add-on drug is started; she has no daytime drowsiness months later she stops it abruptly, with no withdrawal symptoms examination normal → Serotonin 1A receptor partial agonism → buspirone partially stimulates serotonin 1A receptors and brings no sedation, tolerance or dependence; a benzodiazepine sedates and brings withdrawal, and hydroxyzine, a histamine 1 blocker, causes drowsiness
  3. 79-year-old woman with generalized anxiety disorder; sertraline started 2 weeks ago hydroxyzine added 3 days ago for agitation and poor sleep now drowsy, inattentive and confused, with a dry mouth afebrile · no clonus · reflexes normal → Anticholinergic effect of hydroxyzine → a first-generation antihistamine with anticholinergic action can bring on delirium in an older adult; no fever or clonus argues against serotonin syndrome, and onset within days of a new drug argues against dementia
